mappings.note: A word web built from the story's vocabulary. C-2.2-LO-5 is the only outcome about working out word meanings from the way they are used in the text. Not C-1.2: nothing is written from the student's own experience.

An extract ending on 'never seen her cry in the most difficult situations', asking what that tells us about the grandmother. What the reader knows of her comes entirely through the narrator's eyes, which is C-2.2-LO-1. Not C-2.2-LO-3: her determination is not in view here, only the narrator's picture of her.
The extract is her resolve itself -- the Saraswati Puja deadline and 'for learning there is no age bar'. That is the lifelong-learning clause of C-2.2-LO-3 verbatim.
'Identify any five words with prefixes from the story.' C-2.2-LO-5 names prefixed words outright; an exact match and no sibling comes close.
Contrasts 'bought' in simple past with 'had passed' in past perfect. C-2.2-LO-4 is about exactly that tense and what it does to the narrative order. The only grammar-facing outcome in this chapter.

The chapter summary, which is mostly Karmaveera, Kashi Yatre, Triveni and the village's reading habits -- the substance of C-2.1-LO-2. Not C-2.1-LO-1: the summary never asks what separates autobiography from fiction.

A gap-fill on a passage about the National Digital Literacy Mission, which is not the story at all. C-3.1, analysing written material, is the honest fit; no C-2.x outcome applies to a text outside the chapter.

A passage on cultural literacy and the CCRT, on India's traditions, languages and arts. C-4.2 covers appreciating that heritage. Not C-4.1, which is about the multilingual make-up of society rather than cultural practice.

Two halves: notes on cultural literacy (C-4.2), then 'talk to your grandparents and find out which book they enjoy' (C-1.2, writing from one's own and others' experience). Both are genuinely set, so both are cited.

Discourse markers -- 'There's no doubt that...', 'So, to put it in a few words...' -- which are the phrasing of discussion and conclusion. That is C-1.1. Not C-2.2-LO-5, which is about word meaning in the story, not about linking expressions.

Who wrote the story. Authorship is what makes the piece autobiographical rather than invented, which is the distinction C-2.1-LO-1 draws. Not C-2.1-LO-2: nothing about period or language community is asked.

The narrator's age. Twelve against sixty-two is the whole basis of the teacher-student reversal C-2.2-LO-2 traces, which is why this and the grandmother's age both sit there rather than under setting.
The grandmother's name, Krishtakka -- a Kannada name that places the story in its language community, which is what C-2.1-LO-2 asks the student to recognise.
Sixty-two. Paired with b088349ebf23929e: the two ages together are the reversal, so both cite C-2.2-LO-2.
North Karnataka. Place, which C-2.1-LO-2 names directly.
The slow transport of the period. Time and place, and the reason the magazines arrived late -- C-2.1-LO-2's reading habits of that period.
Papers and magazines arriving a day late. Same outcome as the transport question, and for the same reason.
Karmaveera. The magazine is named in C-2.1-LO-2's own wording.
Weekly. The publication rhythm is what made the serialised novel an event in the village -- reading habits of the period.
Kashi Yatre, named in C-2.1-LO-2.
Triveni. The Kannada writer, so again the language community of C-2.1-LO-2.
Kannada. The language community, stated in the outcome.
The plot of Kashi Yatre -- what the serialised novel was about, which C-2.1-LO-2 asks the student to read for what it says about the period.
Kashi. A detail of that same novel.
What shocked the narrator on her return -- her grandmother in tears, which she had never seen. The shock is the narrator's, and the reader feels it through her, so C-2.2-LO-1.
Why she could not read: girls of her generation were not sent to school. Historical context, which is the time clause of C-2.1-LO-2. Not C-2.2-LO-3, which is about what she then does about it.

The realisation that she could not read the magazine on her own -- dependence, and the wound to her self-respect that C-2.2-LO-3 covers. This is the moment 9a49e3cad9cc75aa's history leads to, which is what separates the two.
The Saraswati Puja deadline. Her determination given a date, so C-2.2-LO-3.
How the twelve-year-old first reacted -- she laughed. The narrator's own view again, C-2.2-LO-1, matching 9d4e9db65d8e37e4 in part 1.
